title: Does Your App Need to Work Offline? What to Decide Before You Build

cards.heading: Start with where people use it
cards.text: Trains, car parks and basements are where signal drops. Plan around your customers, not your office Wi-Fi.

cards.heading: List the tasks that must work
cards.text: Name the critical subset, such as viewing today's jobs. Asking for the whole app offline is rarely sensible.

cards.heading: Choose one of three levels
cards.text: Polite failure, read-only, or read and change. Each step is more useful and more work to build.

cards.heading: Decide what happens in a clash
cards.text: If two edits conflict, which one wins? That is a business rule you set before the build.

cards.heading: Think about stored personal data
cards.text: Offline data sits on the phone. Decide what is saved and check data protection rules with an adviser.

facebook.message:
What happens when your customers open your app and the signal drops?
Most apps are planned on fast office Wi-Fi, but used on trains, in car parks and in rural areas. Our latest guide explains what "offline" can mean, three levels of support from a polite error message to full syncing, and the decisions that only you can make, such as what must work without a signal and what happens when two changes clash.
Swipe through for the key points.

To read the full article, visit the FinTaxTech website and find "Does Your App Need to Work Offline? What to Decide Before You Build" in our Blog section.
